newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan has supported the idea of expanding non-permanent membership of the United Nations Security Council.
- Pakistani Foreign Office said the recent outbreak of hostilities in Afghanistan would not affect its shuttle diplomacy.
- Five people of the same family were murdered in Punjab's central town of Gujranwala.
- Pakistan and the International Monetary Fund have agreed to a $1.6 billion enhanced structural adjustment facility loan.
Punjab Chief Minister Shahbaz Sharif has offered to mediate between the two warring sectarian groups.
- Pakistan and India have decided to regularly exchange information on flood discharge and meteorological situation on the telephone twice a day during the current flood season.
- The agreement with the IMF has paved way for foreign investment and upward re-rating of Pakistani economy in global markets, according to financial circles.
- Trade and industry has described the successful conclusion of negotiations between government and IMF for $1.6 billion ESAF/EFF as an endorsement of the economic policies at the global level.

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has said national economy has started giving positive signs during the last four months and added those trying to create law and order situation were in fact not happy with the national development.
